```{js}
$(function() {
  $(".level2").css('visibility', 'hidden');
  $(".level2").first().css('visibility', 'visible');
  $(".container-fluid").height($(".container-fluid").height() + 300);
  $(window).on('scroll', function() {
    $('h2').each(function() {
      var h2Top = $(this).offset().top - $(window).scrollTop();
      var windowHeight = $(window).height();
      if (h2Top >= 0 && h2Top <= windowHeight / 2) {
        $(this).parent('div').css('visibility', 'visible');
      } else if (h2Top > windowHeight / 2) {
        $(this).parent('div').css('visibility', 'hidden');
      }
    });
  });
})
```

## What is my data about?
Well I was curious about my social media habits and engagement with TikTok so i logged data every time I encountered a TikTok while scrolling 📱. Over multiple weeks, through a google form, I recorded the type of content, number of likes, comments, time spent watching, and how I interacted with it. Lets see how much I need to cut down on TikTok 😔


## When am I scrolling the most?

![Bar chart showing the number of TikToks observed by time of day, with categories Morning, Afternoon, Evening, and Night on the x-axis and count on the y-axis](plot1.png)

It wasn't a surprise that the Evening was the peak scrolling period for me. Even though I should be getting most of my work done during that time... as a uni student, mornings are for class, and well evenings, just to take a teeny tiny scrolling break 😆


## What content am I actually interacting with?

![Horizontal bar chart showing the number of TikToks interacted with by content type, ordered from least to most interactions](plot2.png)

Whether it's Code Geass edits, The Mentalist clips, or JoJos memes - Media/Entertainment really does get my attention. Other content like News or Gaming barely gets a look in, and unsurprisingly, advertisements/sponsorships don't even make it onto the plot 🤭


## Does popularity predict how long I watch?

![Scatter plot of number of likes on the x-axis and time spent in seconds on the y-axis, with a linear trend line](plot3.png)

You might expect that if a video has millions of likes, I have to watch it, right? But the data says otherwise... with the adjusted R^2 of 0.001 (close to zero), likes have no relationship with how long I watch TikToks. I guess I'm not a 🐑 after all!


## What did I find out?

I spend way too much time on TikTok, and even more time trying to analyse TikTok

and I think I found a way to stop this addiction ⬇️ ദ്ദി(ᵔᗜᵔ)
